how_claude_should_use_this: For an emergency or situation query, match the user's words against scenarios[].trigger_keywords, then return the matched scenario's steps in order plus any contacts referenced in contacts_needed.

scenarios.title: Guest wants money back from the photo booth
scenarios.context: The photo booth is owned by Western Coin, NOT by Five & Dive. It does not give change (e.g. $20 in, only one $5 strip wanted).
steps: Calmly explain the booth is owned by an outside company (Western Coin) so the venue cannot issue change/refunds from it.
Point to the posted sign/label on the booth explaining no change is given.
Provide the guest the photo booth company's contact number (posted at the booth) for any refund.
De-escalate: offer a small goodwill gesture if the guest is upset (e.g. a complimentary beer) — confirm what they drink before offering.
Do not offer shots/hard liquor if the guest doesn't drink it.
Once calm, let them settle their bill normally.

scenarios.title: Disruptive / intoxicated guest, won't pay or verbally abusive
scenarios.context: Logged case: a young intoxicated guest couldn't pay and verbally assaulted staff; security was called, got him to pay, later arrested him. Separate case: creeps followed a group in and were asked to leave after bothering them.
steps: Stay calm and do not escalate; keep yourself and staff at a safe distance.
If the guest is only disruptive (not violent), ask them to leave once they've settled their bill.
Call mall security for help removing/managing the guest.
If there is a threat to safety, a crime in progress, or violence, call 911.
Let security handle payment recovery and removal; document names/times.
Record the incident in the logbook under 'Any Incidents during PM/AM Shift'.
If individuals are being mall-banned or charged, cooperate with security follow-up (they may return next shift to take statements).

scenarios.title: Electrical fire hazard (frayed/sparking cord or equipment)
scenarios.context: Logged case: stage sound-board power cord was frayed and shooting sparks — flagged as a big fire hazard, photo sent to manager group chat to get it replaced.
steps: Immediately stop using the affected equipment and unplug it if safe to do so.
Isolate the area so guests/staff can't contact it.
If there is active fire or it cannot be made safe, evacuate the area and call 911; use the correct extinguisher only if trained and safe.
Photograph the issue and post in the manager group chat to get it replaced/repaired.
Log it under FOH/BOH Equipment Issues / Maintenance & Repair.
Follow up until replaced — do not return equipment to service until fixed.

scenarios.title: Dishwasher / glasswasher not working (no fill, burning smell, melted switch)
scenarios.context: Logged case: FOH dishwasher wouldn't fill with water and something was burning — a fried switch caused no fill, which overheated the coil (burning smell). Diversity (Diversy) repaired the switch.
steps: Turn the machine off to stop the burning/overheating.
Check the obvious: water supply on, no tripped breaker.
If it won't fill or is burning, do not keep running it — call Diversity (appliance repair) for same-day service; they've fixed this exact fault before.
Switch to manual wash / triple-sink for glassware in the interim.
Log under FOH Equipment Issues / Maintenance & Repair and note in manager-to-manager.

scenarios.title: Draught/draft lines need calibration, cleaning, or pouring problems
scenarios.context: Draught line calibration/cleaning and pouring system handled by Pour Control (Peter) / Sprint Pour Controls; Paul does the calibration visits.
steps: Confirm keg level and CO2/gas before assuming a line fault.
For calibration, cleaning, or persistent pour issues, contact Pour Control — Peter is the main contact; Paul handles calibration scheduling.
Schedule the visit and note it in the logbook.
If the pour/oz meters stop reading: check the plugs and power-cycle the Sprint metering box to reset; it may take a couple of tries before the meter system comes back. (Logged Mar 2/4/7.)

scenarios.title: Food quality complaint (off taste/smell, overcooked, poor presentation)
scenarios.context: Logged case: guest said scotch egg smelled/tasted off; taquitos overcooked; a grilled cheese looked too poor to serve (refused by server, refired). Treated as chef/kitchen error, not an ordering error.
steps: Apologize and take the complaint seriously; pull the item immediately.
Fire a replacement if the guest wants one (refire); verify quality before it leaves the pass.
If it's a kitchen/chef error (not the guest changing their mind), remove the item from the bill.
Tell the closing BOH manager so they can address it with the line cooks.
Log under Kitchen / Food Issues and note coaching follow-up.
If the guest is a first-timer or came in from marketing (e.g. saw us on Global TV), extra care to save the experience.

scenarios.title: Kitchen ticket / bill times running long
scenarios.context: Target bill times in logs are roughly 5–12 min AM, 5–10/15 min PM. Logged spike: corn dogs and a 'crazy bread' each took ~30 min on separate occasions despite a light board.
steps: Check the board/ticket load — is the delay justified by volume?
If times are out of line with the board, the BOH manager speaks to the line directly.
Communicate delays to affected tables proactively.
Log the spike under Kitchen / Food Issues and Bill Times for the shift.

scenarios.title: POS end-of-night batch / report won't print ('no totals available')
scenarios.context: Logged case: batch was closed but printing returned 'no totals available, try again later.'
steps: Re-attempt the print after a short wait (the terminal may need time to settle).
Confirm the batch actually closed before re-batching to avoid double-batching.
If it still fails, note it in Payroll/Cash Issues and flag in manager-to-manager notes for the next manager / head office.
Keep the EOD reports requirement in mind (logbook asks 'Were all end-of-night reports run').

If the internet is down, end-of-night reports / terminal totals may not run at all (logged Mar 18). Try restarting the modem/router; if it can't be restored, note that totals weren't printed and follow up with head office / the POS provider the next day.

scenarios.title: Staff family emergency mid-shift
scenarios.context: Logged case: Sarica was cut at 9:15pm for a family emergency; remaining BOH staff redistributed to cover line/dish.
steps: Release the employee immediately and supportively.
Redistribute their station among remaining staff (move prep to line, manager covers dish/expo as needed).
Note the early cut and reason in the cut list and shift summary.
Check labour coverage for the rest of the night and adjust cuts accordingly.

scenarios.title: Cooler/freezer temperature & frost checks (food safety)
scenarios.context: Standard logged ranges: Kitchen cooler ~2–3C; Kitchen freezer ~ -21 to -22C; Line coolers ~2–3C; Bar cooler ~2C. Checks logged at Open / Switchover / Close. Also check for frost on coils/vents/fans, that fans above cooler run, and the ice machine is free of ice build-up. A historic heating issue above the cooler was solved with an inline fan.
steps: Record temps at Open, Switchover, and Close.
Kitchen cooler/line coolers should read ~2–3C; freezer ~ -21 to -22C; bar cooler ~2C.
If readings are out of range, move product to a working unit and flag maintenance.
Check coils/vents/fans for frost; confirm fans above cooler are running; confirm ice machine is free of build-up.
Log all readings in the End of Night Closing section.

scenarios.title: Duebacks (DB) / cash handling at cashout
scenarios.context: Duebacks (DBs) are routinely given to servers/bartenders at cashout and logged by name/count under Payroll/Cash Issues (e.g. 'Gave DBs to Kayla x1, Carrington x2').
steps: Record each dueback by employee name and count under Payroll / Cash Issues.
Note if the manager took their own DB.
Reconcile against the batch/EOD reports.

scenarios.title: Food complaint comes back — who remakes it (Rule of 3)
scenarios.context: After grilled-cheese quality complaints, management reinforced the 'Rule of 3' and that when a complaint comes in and food comes back, the Manager on Duty (MOD) must personally cook the remake. Managers must keep 'aces in their places'.
steps: Pull the complained-about item immediately.
The Manager on Duty (MOD) personally cooks the remake — not the line cook who made the original.
Verify quality at the pass before it goes out.
If it's a kitchen/chef error, remove the item from the bill.
Have an individual coaching conversation with the cook(s) involved, referencing company standards and the Rule of 3.
Log under Kitchen/Food Issues and BOH Employee Situations.

scenarios.title: Wrong liquid served to guest (e.g. cleaning solution in a water glass)
scenarios.context: Logged case: two waters went out containing vinegar from a bar cleaning jug. Guests did not drink them. Tables were comped soda and were fine.
steps: Remove the affected glasses from the table immediately and confirm whether the guest drank any.
If a guest ingested any chemical/cleaning solution, treat as a medical concern — get them water, monitor, and call 911 / Poison Control if they show any symptoms.
Apologize sincerely and comp affected items/drinks.
Identify the root cause: never store cleaning solution in unlabeled drink-style jugs at the bar; separate and clearly label all chemical containers.
Coach the staff involved.
Log under Service Issues.

scenarios.title: Removing a non-compliant patron (vaping/cut off/refusing to leave) — security & police
scenarios.context: Logged cases: a woman vaping at the bar hid from security, raised her voice, refused to leave; security waited outside, came in to remove her, then had to call police when she verbally harassed and went after a guard. Other removals: barefoot on dancefloor after warnings; a cut-off guest taking shots meant for the band.
steps: Give clear verbal warnings for the behaviour (e.g. no vaping, must wear footwear, already cut off).
If the behaviour continues, inform the guest they must leave.
Call security to assist with removal; have them stage nearby if you anticipate resistance.
If the guest refuses to leave, becomes aggressive, or harasses/assaults staff or security, call 911 / police.
Do not physically engage; let security and police handle removal.
Document names, times, and actions in Incidents (PM/AM Shift).

scenarios.title: Guest upset about cleanliness (dirty menus / cloudy glassware)
scenarios.context: Logged cases: a guest lost it over dirty menus, refused to pay for her pop and walked out before staff could fix it. Separately, cloudy glassware is a recurring issue — scrubber kept on the side; staff scrub glasses before putting away.
steps: Apologize immediately and offer to replace the item (clean menus / fresh glass) right away.
If the guest leaves before you can fix it, don't chase a confrontation; note it and move on.
Preventive: wipe/sanitize all menus before they go to tables (assign to host/server).

Preventive for glassware: scrub cloudy glasses before storing; if glasses are persistently cloudy, this points to the glasswasher (see dishwasher/glasswasher scenario) — check detergent/rinse and call Diversity if needed.
Log under Service Issues.

scenarios.title: Walk-in freezer/cooler reading warm (door not sealed / filter)
scenarios.context: Logged case: walk-in freezer was at +10C because the door wasn't closed properly. BOH did maintenance and changed the fibreglass filter; temp returned to normal (no outside servicing needed). A written warning was issued to the manager responsible for the unsealed door.
steps: Confirm the door is fully closed and sealing; this is the most common cause.
Check product — if anything has thawed/warmed beyond safe range, assess for disposal per food-safety rules.
Inspect/replace the fibreglass filter and clear any frost on coils/fans; allow the unit to recover and re-check temp.
If temp doesn't recover after the door is sealed and filter checked, escalate to refrigeration service.
Record the incident and corrective action in BOH Equipment Issues and temp logs.
If staff negligence caused it, document a coaching/written warning.

scenarios.title: Scheduled hood-vent cleaning — early kitchen close procedure
scenarios.context: Logged: hood vents were blast-cleaned overnight. Kitchen closed early (~10:00-10:30pm to 11pm); the closing BOH manager stayed to let the hood cleaners in and used downtime for pizza dough + extra cleaning.
steps: Confirm the booked cleaning time in advance and note it in the pre-shift focus.
Plan an early kitchen close around the cleaning window and inform FOH so service is communicated to guests.
Closing BOH manager stays to let the hood cleaners in and secures the kitchen.
Use downtime productively (prep/dough/cleaning).
Update the compliance calendar — hood inspection/cleaning was due June 2026.

scenarios.title: Staff attendance problems / resignation / turnover handling
scenarios.context: Logged cases: a BOH employee (Sarica) repeatedly left shifts/called in and was asked to resign; an employee who called in sick was asked for a doctor's note; a manager got a written warning for the freezer door; a server (Destiny) gave notice to move to another venue.
steps: For repeated attendance/communication issues, document each instance with dates in BOH/FOH Employee Situations.
For a call-in sick, you may request a doctor's note, especially if patterns emerge.
For a serious or repeated lapse, issue a written warning and confirm the employee understands.
If issues persist and the fit is wrong, have the formal conversation (up to requesting resignation) — document it.
When someone gives notice, note it and start the rehire/onboarding pipeline (interviews, Push invite, references).
Keep labour covered by adjusting cuts/on-call when someone is out.

scenarios.title: POS / cash system malfunction (terminals, payments, Star Cash)
scenarios.context: Logged: a multi-hour Star Cash support call resolved a POS/cash malfunction; system tested multiple times afterward. Also relevant to the earlier batch-print 'no totals available' issue.
steps: Confirm the scope — one terminal or all? Network/internet up?
Restart the affected terminal if safe.
Call Star Cash for POS/cash system support; expect to work through it live with them.
Test thoroughly (multiple transactions) before relying on it again.
Keep a manual fallback for taking payment if the system is fully down.
Log under Payroll/Cash Issues and flag in manager-to-manager notes.

If a POS station's login button/screen disappears (e.g. right-side stage terminal, Feb 8): try restarting that terminal a few times; if it doesn't return, use another station and flag for POS/Pixel support.

scenarios.title: Health inspector spotted / inspection readiness
scenarios.context: Logged: a health inspector was spotted on Bourbon St; BOH did extra cleaning and confirmed temp logs are backdated to Nov 2025, so they're ready for inspection at any time.
steps: Keep temp logs current and complete at all times (backdated records were maintained to Nov 2025).
If an inspector is spotted nearby, do a quick extra clean and verify logs/labels/dates are in order.
Confirm food handling permits and business licence are valid (both good to Sept 2026).
Confirm fire suppression (due May 26) and hood cleaning (due June) are current.
Be courteous and cooperative; provide records on request.

scenarios.title: Guest refuses to pay for a duplicate/disputed order
scenarios.context: Logged case: a guest ordered the same item from two servers, it was made twice, she refused to pay the second and left. The second drinks hadn't hit the table so they were resold; no loss. She returned later and paid as she went.
steps: Stay calm; don't force the dispute if the guest is leaving.
If the duplicate never reached the table, resell it — no loss to recover.
Briefly explain you'll take care of it; if the guest won't engage, let it go gracefully.
Prevent recurrence: confirm orders and avoid two servers taking from the same table (clear section ownership).
Log under Service Issues if notable.

scenarios.title: Bar equipment fixes (bill printer, soda gun nozzle)
scenarios.context: Logged: Brent (BOH) fixed the bar bill printer in-house. A new nozzle for the back-bar soda gun was ordered (via Coke rep).
steps: For the bill printer: check paper, connection, and power; a manager (Brent has done this) can often fix in-house before calling support.
For a worn/clogged soda gun nozzle: order a replacement nozzle through the Coke/soft-drink rep.
Log under FOH Equipment Issues / Maintenance & Repair.

scenarios.title: Bar/payment terminal malfunctioning (debit-credit machine)
scenarios.context: Logged: the bar payment machine ('Stevie') malfunctioned; Moneris was called and sent a tech the next afternoon.
steps: Confirm whether it's one terminal or all, and whether the network/internet is up.
Restart the terminal if safe.
Call Moneris for payment-terminal support; they can dispatch a tech.
Use another working terminal in the meantime; keep a manual fallback for taking payment.
Log under FOH Equipment Issues and note in manager-to-manager.
(If the issue is the cash system rather than the card terminal, that's Star Cash; if it's the POS software/buttons, see POS scenarios.)

scenarios.title: VLT / gaming machine error (bill acceptor jam) — AGLC
scenarios.context: Logged: a VLT (the one whose screen faces the front door, in the '30s' area) threw a 'bill acceptor jammed' error that staff couldn't clear.
steps: Do not force the bill acceptor; take the machine out of use.
Try the basic reset if your AGLC procedures allow, otherwise leave it.
Call AGLC the next morning to report and get the VLT serviced.
Log under FOH Equipment Issues / Maintenance & Repair.

scenarios.title: Guest mishandling alcohol (pouring multiple shots into one cup / over-serving)
scenarios.context: Logged: a guest ordered 10 tequila shots and poured all into one cup to drink. Staff explained AGLC rules allow only 3 drinks in front of a guest at once; guest became hostile, security removed him (his wife escalated the scene).
steps: Inform the guest of the AGLC limit: only ~3 drinks may be in front of one person at a time.
Offer to hold the remaining drinks behind the bar to serve in rounds.
If the guest refuses and becomes hostile, stop further service.
Call security to assist; clear a path/chairs so they can remove the guest safely.
Don't physically engage; let security handle removal and call police if it escalates.
Document the incident with time and details.

scenarios.title: Guest medically incapacitated / needs EMS
scenarios.context: Logged: a wheelchair-bound patron became incoherent after three drinks over an extended period and could not leave; mall security spoke with her and she was eventually taken by EMS.
steps: Stop all further alcohol service immediately.
Stay with the guest, keep them safe, and monitor responsiveness.
If the guest is incoherent, unresponsive, or cannot safely leave, call EMS (911) without delay.
Involve mall security to help manage the area and access.
Arrange safe transport (EMS, sober driver, or cab) — never let an incapacitated guest leave on their own.
Document the time, what was served over what period, and actions taken.

scenarios.title: Guest disputes portion size / refuses to pay (becomes hostile)
scenarios.context: Logged: a guest claimed his pineapple chicken balls + rice portion was too small and refused to pay; he'd eaten everything, became aggressive ('are you challenging me'), then paid and left flipping everyone off. Portions are weighed to standard.
steps: Stay calm and professional; do not match hostility.
Explain that portions are weighed to a set standard — that's how the item is served.
Ask to see the dish; if it's been fully eaten, there's no quality issue to remedy.
If the guest is just dissatisfied with standard portion (not an error), you are within rights to decline to adjust the bill — say so politely.
If the guest becomes threatening, disengage and involve security.
Don't escalate; let them settle and leave. Log under Service Issues if notable.

scenarios.title: Intoxicated/erratic guest at the bar (drinking others' drinks, harassing staff)
scenarios.context: Multiple logged cases: a male too intoxicated sat at random tables and drank a stranger's beer; a young man poked customers and lured one toward the washroom, refused to pay (security dragged him out), returned later wired and was mall-banned 24h; a woman harassed a bartender about a hair bow, called staff names, refused to leave and got a 24h mall ban.
steps: Refuse further service the moment intoxication or erratic/harassing behaviour appears.
Give a clear instruction to settle up and leave.
Call security early — don't wait for it to escalate; have them stage nearby.
Keep staff and other guests at a safe distance; do not physically engage.
Security handles removal and can issue mall bans (commonly 24h); police if it escalates.
Record a description, time, and outcome (incl. any mall ban) in Incidents.

scenarios.title: Patio live music shut down by mall (noise complaints / lease rules)
scenarios.context: Logged: patio live music drew an instant crowd but mall security shut it down within ~25 min citing complaints from other restaurants, an '8-foot rule', and a lease clause that live music must come from the stage only — even after volume was lowered and performers moved inside.
steps: If mall security raises a complaint, lower volume and cooperate in the moment.
Know the lease terms: live music may be restricted to the indoor stage only — confirm before booking patio performances.
Don't argue with security on the floor; comply and escalate the policy question to ownership/head office afterward.
Document what was said (rules cited, times) for the head-office conversation.
Re-route performers to the approved stage area to keep the music going.

scenarios.title: Building issue: plumbing (urinal/flood) or cooler door — mall maintenance
scenarios.context: Logged: urinal was fixed by mall maintenance, then flooded and needed a snake; cooler door handle/part needed a fix but couldn't be done on a stat holiday (maintenance off).
steps: For building/plumbing/structural issues, call Mall Maintenance first.
Note that mall maintenance is typically OFF on stat holidays — plan to call back the next business day.
For a flooding fixture, shut off/limit use of that fixture and contain water until they arrive.
Log under FOH Equipment Issues / Maintenance & Repair and leave a manager-to-manager note if it carries to the next day.

scenarios.title: Cash float discrepancy at open/close
scenarios.context: Logged: floats were 'out' one night but resolved — the issue was inaccurate bill bundles. Cash team and managers must verify every bundle. Cash overages are returned to staff (e.g. Hugo's overage).
steps: Recount the float carefully; the common culprit is a mis-counted bundle of bills.
Have the cash team AND a manager both verify each bundle.
If a server has an overage/shortage, reconcile it (overages returned to the employee).
Document under Payroll/Cash Issues; flag in manager-to-manager notes if unresolved.

scenarios.title: Server order-entry errors causing voids / wrong items
scenarios.context: Logged: a newer server kept generating voids by not reviewing orders before hitting send; coached to slow down and match the ticket to what was written before sending. Also reinforced urgency/steps of service.
steps: Coach the server to review each order against their written notes before hitting send.
Reinforce a sense of urgency and steps of service (greet within the 1-minute rule, table maintenance).
Document the coaching conversation in Employee Situations; track for improvement within probation (90 days).
Teach recovery skills too (e.g. how to reprint a lost CC slip from the terminal).

scenarios.title: Pest sighting (mice) — traps & sanitation
scenarios.context: Logged: mouse droppings found behind the office safe (causing a smell — no live/dead mice found there); later a mouse was caught on a trap set by staff/Atlas and removed. Pest control (Rentokil) reports are actioned.
steps: Clean and sanitize any droppings immediately (gloves; proper disinfectant); locate and seal the source if possible.
Set traps in affected areas.
Ensure all food is stored sealed and off the floor; dated and rotated.
Action all recommendations from the Rentokil pest-control report.
Keep records for health-inspection readiness; log under BOH/Employee Situations or Equipment as appropriate.

scenarios.title: Staff member feels faint / collapses on shift (e.g. heatstroke in a hot kitchen)
scenarios.context: Logged Apr 30: a BOH staff member got dizzy in a warm prep hall and fainted (heatstroke). Manager filed an incident report, sent them home, and asked them to check in the next day.
steps: Stop the staff member's work immediately and get them to a cool, safe place to sit or lie down.
Check responsiveness. If unconscious, not breathing normally, having a seizure, or not recovering quickly, call 911 right away.
Cool them down and give water if they are alert and able to drink; loosen tight clothing; do not leave them alone.
If they recover and it was heat-related, relieve them for the day and arrange a safe ride home — do not let them drive if still unwell.
Fill out an incident report documenting time, symptoms, cause (e.g. kitchen heat), and action taken.
Follow up the next day; address the root cause (kitchen ventilation/heat, hydration, breaks) to prevent recurrence.

scenarios.title: Assault / fight — a guest is attacked or two guests fight (incl. at the entrance)
scenarios.context: Logged Mar 9: a guest (Loredo) seated on the bench outside an entrance was punched in the face unprovoked by another man; security and police were called, police took a statement, and staff gave the victim first aid (ice/napkins) and advised a hospital check. Mar 14 also saw a couple fight and run out after ordering.
steps: Ensure your own safety first; do not physically intervene in an active fight — separate verbally and create space.
Call mall security immediately, and call 911 (police/EMS) if anyone is hurt, a weapon is involved, or the aggressor won't disengage.
Tend to the victim: basic first aid (ice, clean napkins for bleeding), keep them calm, and advise medical attention / hospital even if they seem okay.
Try to keep the aggressor contained for security/police if it's safe to do so; otherwise note description and direction of travel.
Preserve any information for police: witness names, what was seen, timestamps, and camera locations.
Write an incident report with time, people involved, what happened, and actions taken; note the police/security file if one was opened.

scenarios.title: Mall lockdown — drill or real (shelter in place / secure the space)
scenarios.context: Logged Feb 4 (scheduled) and Feb 11 (drill ran AM & PM). West Edmonton Mall runs periodic lockdown drills; staff should know the difference between a drill and a real event and how to respond.
steps: Confirm whether it's a scheduled drill or a real lockdown (mall security / mall PA / management). Treat as real until told otherwise.
Follow mall security's direction. In a real lockdown: stop seating/serving at the entrance, keep guests inside and calm, and secure or monitor the entrance(s) as instructed.
Do not let guests leave into the mall if security has called a hold; keep them comfortable and informed without causing panic.
Account for staff; keep the team together and away from entrances/windows if there's a threat.
Wait for the all-clear from mall security before resuming normal entry/exit.
After a drill or event, note the time and any issues in the logbook.

scenarios.title: A guest's property (wallet, phone, bag) is stolen on site
scenarios.context: Seen Jan 30 2026: a guest's wallet contents were stolen on pub side. Mall security handles theft investigations on mall property; the venue's job is to act fast, preserve a description, and connect the guest to security.
steps: Stay calm and reassure the guest; take the report seriously and immediately.
Call mall security right away and brief them (location, time, what was taken).
Get a description of any suspect from the guest and any witnesses at the table while it is fresh.
If safe, do a quick check of the immediate area / nearby venues (e.g. Hudson's, Bag o' Crab) - do NOT pursue or confront a suspect yourself.
Bring security to the affected table so the guest can give them the description and details directly; let security take it from there.
Check whether the bathroom-hallway cameras (flagged historically as not working) or any working cameras cover the area; note this for the owner.
Log the incident with time, guest contact, and what was reported.

scenarios.title: A guest gropes, grabs, or harasses a staff member
scenarios.context: Seen Jan 2 2026: an intoxicated birthday guest (already on a final strike) grabbed a server and demanded a kiss; the server was frightened. Staff were removed quickly. Touching staff is never tolerated, regardless of how the guest's table reacts. Cross-venue note (Dec 19 2025): a regular ('Nick') was permanently banned from BOTH Five & Dive and the neighbouring Hudson's after sexually assaulting a server at Hudson's - venues on Bourbon St share information and coordinate bans on guests who assault staff anywhere on the strip.
steps: Get the affected staff member to safety immediately and check on them; their wellbeing comes first.
Have a manager or door/security remove the offending guest right away - do not wait for further incidents.
Be clear and firm that touching or harassing staff is not allowed and is grounds for immediate removal.
If the guest resists or escalates, call mall security; if there is an assault, call police (911).
Address the guest's table calmly but firmly that the behaviour is unacceptable, especially toward staff; do not argue if they downplay it.
Settle the table's bill and let them leave; consider a ban for the offending guest.
Support the staff member afterward (offer a break, check if they want to report to police) and log the incident with names, time, and witnesses.

scenarios.title: A minor / underage guest is on the premises or in a party
scenarios.context: Seen Dec 7 2025: a table brought a minor in and had to be asked to leave. Five & Dive is an AGLC-licensed premises; minors are not permitted in licensed areas even if not drinking. The law applies regardless of how the guest's party reacts.
steps: Check ID if there is any doubt about age; AGLC rules require valid government photo ID.
If a minor is present in the licensed area, politely but firmly explain they cannot stay - it is an AGLC legal requirement, not a venue preference.
Ask the party to leave or relocate the minor; do not serve alcohol to or near the minor.
Stay calm if the party is upset (they may threaten a bad review) - document the interaction and that the law was followed.
If anyone refuses to leave or escalates, call mall security; never serve a suspected minor.
Log the incident with time and details.

external_factors_seen: Mall close time shifts late-night traffic (e.g. Bourbon Street closing pushed guests over).
Oilers playoff results affect volume (elimination slowed business).
Global TV segment/feature drives walk-ins ('saw us on Global').
Weather logged daily and correlates with patio/volume.
Warm weather pulls crowds to Whyte Ave patios and golf, hurting indoor bar traffic (Bourbon St 'dead').
Ice palace / nearby events can drive later foot traffic.
Tuesday after a long weekend reliably slows down.
Mall closing early kills late-night business.
Mall closing early (e.g. 6pm on stat holidays) sharply cuts evening business.
Comedy club next door releases waves of guests to stage side after shows.
Oilers games, concerts, and 'checking out the mall' bring out-of-towners.
Bourbon St ('BRBN') closing pushes industry crowd over at last call.
Repeat problem patrons (e.g. comes in only to play VLTs, spits/throws things, runs out on bills) — track and ban at the door; mall security and police back this up.
Nearby competitor closing (e.g. Hudson's last weekend / running out of stock) sends overflow and nostalgia crowds our way.
Daylight Savings clock change shifts late-night timing (e.g. jump straight to 3am).
Big ticketed shows (e.g. The Hip) and VIP-ticket pushes drive pre-event traffic and spender groups.
Hudson's permanent closure became an ongoing weekend driver (pub side jammed by early afternoon) — start times adjusted up for weekends.
BC reading week brought extra traffic.
Major sporting events (Olympics, Super Bowl, Leafs/Oilers games) pull guests home or downtown; expect a slow lead-up and a post-event push (incl. VLT play).
Family Day long weekend + in-mall hockey tournaments lift daytime/weekend traffic.
Heavy snow days sharply cut volume (only die-hards come in).
U of A booking the WEM waterpark brings student traffic in and out.
Concerts at Rogers Place (e.g. Megadeth, Big Wreck, Econoline Crush, Live) pull crowds downtown but can send an after-show rush to WEM.
Extreme cold snaps (-25) keep the pub-side BRBN doors closed and can drive pest activity (Rentokil spot inspections).
Tragically Hip cover-band weekend promoted as a draw (marquee/table-topper push).
Hudson's (nearby competitor) cut to reduced hours in early Jan 2026 (closing 1am Fri/Sat, 11pm Sun-Thu) before its mid-March closure - Five & Dive picked up a few more late-night tables even then.
Major Rogers Place / arena events (e.g. the Shoresy Classic, Jan 23-24 2026) and Oilers games drive large day/late-night spikes.
Bourbon Street safety incidents (e.g. a Jan 29 2026 gunshot near Boston Pizza triggering a mall lockdown and police street closure) can shut down late-night traffic entirely.
Concerts and big shows (e.g. Offspring, Jan 30 2026) plus sold-out comedy-club and Waterpark University events drive strong late-night spikes.
Mall food-court security incidents (e.g. a Jan 26 2026 fake-gun report) can trigger a sudden full mall lockdown mid-service - guests must be moved to the back hallway fast.
Extreme cold (e.g. -22 on Dec 12 2025) suppresses turnout - large reservations no-show or arrive at half size because people won't drive in.
Holiday calendar drives the daytime mall 'shot therapy' trade (Christmas Eve) and early closes (Dec 24 closed after ~3pm); Boxing Day specials and NYE ticketed events are major December levers.
Out-of-town Oilers-game visitors (e.g. Winnipeg fans Dec 5 2025) boost weekend volume.
Pre-Christmas Fridays/weekends are the year's peak (Dec 6 ~$18.5k, Dec 19 ~$15.8k, Dec 20 ~$15.1k) - heavy live music, large parties and a rowdier 'holiday' crowd needing more removals.
Freezing rain / extreme cold and bad roads thin large reservations (parties show at a fraction of their booking) even when the mall itself is busy.
Oilers Stanley Cup Final games drive (and distort) volume: the bar empties during play and fills as the game wraps; deep playoff runs bring a rowdier 'riff raff' crowd.

Canada Day long weekend reliably slows the downtown/Bourbon St strip (people travel/take days off); out-of-town tournament teams (e.g. the Brick tournament) backfill late-night traffic as the rest of the strip closes.
Hosting large out-of-town tournament groups (Brick tournament) brings buffet catering and parent/spectator overflow.
Calgary Stampede (early-mid July) pulls regional crowds away and softens mid-week/weekend traffic.
Major concerts (e.g. Weezer) and the race track draw potential guests elsewhere on big event nights.
After a major in-house fight, Bourbon St venues banned the involved out-of-town group (e.g. Brick-tournament parents), measurably slowing the strip for days afterward.
Out-of-town summer tourists (e.g. US visitors on vacation) seen mid-week may return on the weekend.
MLB World Series Game 7 (Blue Jays) was kept staffed for in case of a win-driven rush; the Jays lost so the rush never materialized (Nov 1 2025).
Concerts at Rogers Place (e.g. Brad Paisley, Nov 7) and a rodeo in town (Nov 15) can drive late traffic - sometimes a hoped-for post-event rush does not arrive.
Hudson's (nearby competitor) was still operating in early-mid November 2025 (product loans both ways, closing ~11pm) - confirms it had not yet closed.
First snowfall of the year (Nov 7) slowed lunch trade.
Grey Cup (CFL final, Nov 16) and an in-town rodeo brought extra lunch/viewing traffic.
Remembrance Day (Nov 11 stat holiday) brought a busy daytime crowd (military uniforms, groups) but closed mall maintenance for the day.
Black Friday (Nov 28) drove a big night with walk-in Christmas-party groups.
Hudson's and Boston Pizza staff/patrons cross over to F&D after their shifts (e.g. quiet Nov 16 night kept lively by them).
K-Days / large downtown events (and the Stampede) pull crowds away from WEM and soften F&D sales, even in summer.
Sports tournaments at the mall/arena (e.g. youth hockey tournaments) can spike or, when they end, drop traffic from out-of-town/hotel guests.
